subject: Usage spike reconciliation & commit extension proposal
messages:
From: Hemant Singh <hemant@opsly.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Opsly Finance <finance@opsly.com>, Rachel Park <rachel@opsly.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden June spike — need reconciliation and next steps

Diego,

We saw a large, unexpected jump in inference hours on June 12–15 that pushed us well over our committed capacity. Our finance team pulled the attached usage report and flagged ~220k extra inference hours that we didn't forecast. We need to reconcile ASAP to understand root cause and agree next steps for settlement.

Questions from Opsly finance:
- Can Redwood confirm these hours and provide a usage breakdown by project/route?
- We prefer avoiding an immediate one-off invoice if possible — is there room to apply a one-time credit and roll the remainder into a short-term top-up or commit extension?
- If a charge is required, can payment terms be net 60?

I've copied Rachel and finance so we can coordinate. Appreciate a quick call if helpful — we can be available 11:00–13:00 PT today.

Thanks,
Hemant Singh
Head of Platform
Opsly

Attachment: opsly-usage-report-Jun2027.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Hemant Singh <hemant@opsly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>, Opsly Finance <finance@opsly.com>, Rachel Park <rachel@opsly.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden June spike — need reconciliation and next steps

Hemant — thanks for the heads up and for the attached report. We've pulled the usage on our side and see the same elevated token/inference-hour pattern around June 12–15. Early observation: high KV-cache misses on your main inference route plus a batch-job that retried a large backfill over that window.

Proposed short plan: 
1) I will share an annotated usage breakdown (project/route) by EOD today.
2) Ben (cc'd) can propose commercial remedies: one-off credit + short commit extension or a split invoice + deferred payment.
3) If Opsly is open, we can offer a temporary safety cap and an autoscaling guard to prevent repeats while the backfill finishes.

Would you like to take the 11:00 PT slot for a quick screen-share? If so, Ben and I will join.

--
Diego Fernandez
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Hemant Singh <hemant@opsly.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>, Opsly Finance <finance@opsly.com>, Rachel Park <rachel@opsly.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden June spike — need reconciliation and next steps

Hemant — thanks for raising this. I joined the 11:00 PT call and wanted to summarize commercial options we discussed so Opsly can pick a path forward quickly. (Diego will send the per-route breakdown shortly.)

Option A — Goodwill credit + short-term top-up
- Redwood issues a one-time goodwill credit of 20% of the excess usage value (applied to the June invoice).
- Remaining 80% of the excess can be converted into a 3-month top-up commitment at a 10% discounted rate vs on-demand.
- No immediate cash outlay by Opsly; invoice reflects post-credit amount with standard net 30 terms.

Option B — Split invoice + deferred payment
- Redwood issues an invoice for the full excess usage amount.
- Opsly can elect net 60 on that invoice and sign a 6-month commit extension at current pricing to avoid future spikes.

Option C — One-time amortized charge + commit extension
- Redwood amortizes the excess over 3 invoices (equal installments) and OPSLY signs a 12-month incremental commit which includes a 5% price concession on the incremental capacity.

We tried to prioritize minimizing disruption to Opsly's cash flow while recognizing the overage. If Opsly prefers, we can also combine elements (e.g., smaller credit + longer amortization). Please indicate preferred option and I'll get finance/legal to prep the paperwork and an updated invoice draft.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Hemant Singh <hemant@opsly.com>, Opsly Finance <finance@opsly.com>, Rachel Park <rachel@opsly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden June spike — need reconciliation and next steps

Hemant / Rachel — follow-up with the reconciled breakdown attached. Key points: 
- Verified excess: 223,890 inference hours (June 12–15) tied to two routes: /inference/billing-backfill (71%) and /inference/realtime-search (29%).
- Root cause: a scheduled backfill job retried unexpectedly after transient failure; the KV-cache config for billing-backfill caused low reuse across retries.

Commercial resolution we prepared: 
- Redwood credit: 25% goodwill credit on the excess usage (applied to June invoice).
- Opsly commit extension: Opsly signs a 4-month incremental commit equal to 60% of the excess (spread across the 4 months) at a 7% discounted rate.
- Billing: Redwood will issue a proposed invoice reflecting the credit and amortized commit; Opsly can elect net 60 on the residual balance.

Attachments: redwood-proposed-invoice-INV-4879.pdf (PDF, 32KB) and the reconciled usage CSV.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm Opsly's acceptance of the proposed credit + 4-month extension by EOD Tue 29 Jun so we can lock pricing and issue the invoice.
2) If accepted, we'll run a short config change to add an autoscale safety cap for billing-backfill routes and provide a small postmortem summary of mitigation steps.

If you want a final 20–30m call to walk the invoice, Ben can join and Logan will cover technical mitigations.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-proposed-invoice-INV-4879.pdf, opsly-usage-report-Jun2027.csv
